kanca: A 25-foot molasses wave smashed Boston's streets.
cumleler: A 25-foot molasses wave smashed Boston's streets.
On January 15, 1919, the Purity tank burst.
Temperatures rose above 40 degrees Fahrenheit, possibly expanding the molasses.
At 12:30 p.m., the tank collapsed, unleashing a 35 mph surge.
The wave knocked a streetcar off its tracks.
Cadets from USS Nantucket waded in, rescuing trapped victims.
Even summer days still smelled of molasses in Boston.

Front of the Purity Distilling Company tank at 529 Commercial Street, winter sky, steam rising, a few workers in wool coats watching, camera centered on the massive steel cylinder.
Side profile of the cylindrical tank, height markers showing 50 ft, diameter markers showing 90 ft, a man with a clipboard standing beside it, camera eye-level.
Thermometer on a fence reading 40°F, sun low on horizon, faint heat ripples above the tank, workers wiping sweat from foreheads, camera wide shot.
Tank bursting, rivets flying, a dark wave bursting forth at high speed, camera from street level looking toward the explosion, a Cadet in navy uniform just entering frame.
Streetcar tipped onto its side, tracks bending, molasses swirling around, a horse-drawn cart nearby, camera angled from the side of the street.
Group of three navy-uniformed Cadets waist-deep in sticky molasses, pulling a small child out, other rescued people clinging to a brick wall, camera over the shoulder of a Cadet.
Modern summer street in Boston's North End, golden light, faint golden haze drifting over the sidewalk, a lone woman pausing with a hand near her nose, camera at eye level.
